verdicts.reason: Both quotes verified verbatim in one file. opportunities-casting-cx.md:45-46 reads '...publication `bump` must not re-fire either — one alert per post per subscriber, ever.' and :66 reads 'Publication is the fan-out's sole trigger; bump and edit are excluded by rule (D-13). Targeting-widening is the only legal cause of a second alert (cap 2 lifetime per user/post).' The single sentence at :66 excludes 'edit' and then names an edit (targeting-widening) as a legal second alert, and :45-46 caps at one while :66 caps at two. The owning decision 04.02.04-alert-subscriptions-delivery.md:244 (D-12) reads 'Two alerts per (user, post), lifetime' and :149 makes a deadline escalation — a non-publication event — consume alert 2. No marker on either statement. Cap 1 vs cap 2 is a directly divergent build.

Quotes verified: 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md:35 'Outcome | Won / not selected | **Tiered** — accepted, waitlisted, rejected', :45 '5. Tiered dispositions go out — accepted, waitlisted, rejected. All of them (04.05.01).' 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:54-62 enumerates exactly seven values (won, not selected, filled elsewhere, withdrawn by poster, withdrawn by applicant, expired, no-decision) — no 'waitlisted'; 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:212 (D-06) 'The applicant is told **a date, not a state** ... Never "you're a maybe"'. Real unreconciled statement. Downgraded from blocking because the same file resolves it authoritatively at :102 (Q-02, RESOLVED: a waitlisted act is a shortlist rank or a dated hold, and the applicant is told a date) and the States row at :67 explicitly points there ('See Q-02 — the rot state'), so the implementer has an in-file answer; what survives is a stale happy-path/comparison line, not an unanswerable gap.

Quotes are accurate but they are not three lifespans. 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:62-66 is an inactivity rule ('any post with no poster activity for a type-scoped interval — ... 30 days for member-wanted ... At 2× the interval it auto-tombstones'), not a lifespan; :60 is the absolute board exit ('Poster closes it, or 90 days elapse'); and 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:36/:63 ('Open-ended; runs for months' / 'Live, open-ended, no deadline') is a contrast against deadline-bearing types, which 04.02.01:63 itself uses the same way ('never for deadline-bearing types — the deadline *is* the freshness signal'). 90 days is 'months'. The board file owns board lifecycle and states it completely; both readings converge on: no deadline field, stale marker at 30 days of inactivity, tombstone at 60, board exit at 90.

Verified against disk, not against the quote. opportunities-casting-index.md:46 says '5 sub-domains · 22 leaf feature files · 59 Deep Think hypotheses logged' and :85 repeats '22 leaf features'; ideation-index.md:121 says '5 sub-domains + 23 features'. Disk: 23 leaf feature files (21 under the five sub-domains plus 04.06 and 04.07) — so 22 is wrong on both readings. Deep Think rows counted programmatically across those 23 files total 156, not 59. Per-child columns are stale in the same direction: 04.01-opportunity-posting-targeting-index.md:26 says 04.01.01 has '3 hypotheses' against 15 on disk; 04.02-discovery-matching-alerts-index.md:26 says 04.02.01 has '2 hypotheses' against 10. Bookkeeping only — no product behaviour is invented — hence warning.

Tracking is malformed, which the rubric treats as a real Dimension-7 finding rather than a valid deferral. 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:56 and 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md:56 both carry a bare '`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`' with no owner column and no live target, while every row in the same files' Open Questions tables carries Owner plus a live stage (e.g. 04.06:101 'User | /create-prd', :103 'Agent | /create-prd-architecture'). The named target is spent per 04.06:103 ('Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, which has run and left 04.01.02 Q-02 open'). Warning rather than blocking because the 04.07 timezone row is answerable upstream (04.01.01:271 D-10 plus 04.03.01:85); the orphaned-band row at 04.06:56 is the genuinely untracked one.

Both sides verified verbatim and both are normative with no marker. 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:104 'compensation (inherited from the booking)' and :108-109 'The compensation gate evaluates synchronously (CX-01), and passes without interaction because the fee came from the booking.' Against 04.01.03-compensation-spec-work-guardrails.md:223 (D-17) '**Compensation is never pre-filled from the source booking**, even when the post is raised from context (04.01.01 D-02)', :87 same sentence in the Happy Path, and :140 'Date, venue and setlist inherit. **Compensation does not** (DT-15) ... Compensation step is blank and required'. The domain's headline flow is three interactions on one reading and three-plus-a-mandatory-compensation-declaration on the other; an implementer cannot build the composer without choosing.

Quotes accurate but they describe one behaviour. 04.01.01:45-46 reads 'Soft ceiling: **25 slots per post** — past that it is a hiring round, and the shape that serves it is the open call (04.07)' — the same sentence that names the ceiling also states the routing. :148 gives the only concrete behavioural row: 'Refused above 25; routed to the open call shape (04.07)' with copy offering no override, and opportunities-casting-cx.md:29 says the ceiling 'routes here'. The file demonstrates elsewhere that it says 'warn, never block' when it means advisory (D-13 at :274, tier-2 duplicate detection). Every reasonable reading builds refuse-and-route to 04.07; 'soft' characterises the ceiling as a product-shape line, not an unenforced one.

04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:47 does read 'Unresolved and important', but its own Q-01 at :100 resolves it in the same file ('✅ RESOLVED — yes. An explicit invite waives eligibility; the mismatch is shown to the poster on the invite and on the submission, never silently suppressed'), sourced to 04.01.04-eligibility-requirement-criteria.md:102 (D-05) and applied at :58. Substantively the stale row says the same thing — 'honour the invite, show the poster the mismatch'. The only residue is whether the mismatch renders as a confirm prompt or an inline notice, which is presentation, not product behaviour: both implementers ship invite-proceeds-plus-mismatch-shown.

Verified by grep across the whole domain: 'fill window' occurs exactly once, at 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:166 — '`Filled elsewhere` is a **first-class, one-tap terminal action** offered proactively on any post older than its type's typical fill window' — and no value is given for any of the twelve types in the taxonomy table at :76-89 or anywhere else. No open question covers it (04.01.01 Q-01..Q-08). The same file states its other intervals and flags them tunable (D-13 at :274), so the omission is not the file's convention. The dependency is load-bearing per :243 ('the domain's beachhead (D-04) is undeliverable without it'). Warning, not blocking: an implementer can fall back on 04.02.01 D-05/D-06's type-scoped decay intervals, but the trigger is post-age, not inactivity, so the fallback is a guess.

04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:49 verified verbatim: 'Poster targets someone who has blocked them | Invite silently fails — but silently to *whom*? Telling the poster leaks the block. | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — a Trust & Safety (24) boundary.' No owner; the named stage is spent (04.01.02:101 Q-02 'Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5'). The file's three questions at :100-102 cover invite-vs-eligibility (resolved), confidentiality-as-a-property and trusted-network cold start — none covers this. The 04.01 side of the same divergence, quoted accurately: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:128 'The fan-out fires **once per post per subscriber, ever** (D-13)', :198 'alerts fanned out once (D-13)', :240 'Publication is the fan-out's sole trigger, and **bump must not re-fire it** (D-13) — one alert per post per subscriber, ever.' Two normative caps and two disjoint trigger sets, no marker on either.

The quoted line 04.01.01:187 exists but is not the candidate board. The board file owns candidate-facing rendering and settles it: 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:202 (DT-09) rejects candidate-visible applicant counts on values grounds, and :148 places counts in the poster's own affordance ('Their own posts surface in a distinct "Your posts" affordance with applicant counts'). All three verified verbatim as bare markers with no owner: 04.02-discovery-matching-alerts-cx.md:104 (CX-03 q5, replay of suppressed alerts), :143 (CX-05 q3 'Permission intersection: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`') and :146 (CX-05 q5 'State transition conflict:' same marker). Two are recoverable from 04.02.04 (D-11 replay conditions at :138; D-14 at :212 states it answers CX-05's permission question), which is why this is a warning; CX-05 q5 — whether an already-computed Critical tier survives a material-score invalidation — has no answer anywhere in the tree.

Verified verbatim: 04.02.03-material-aware-dep-matching.md:64 '| Stale | Setlist changed post-scoring | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |' and :52 '| Setlist changes after matching | Score invalidated ... `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — **re-score, or accept staleness?**'. The question the finding raises is the one 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:214 already tracks, with a well-formed owner and a live target: 'Q-05 | **Can one post carry more than one role/chair?** (D-05, DT-05.) ... This is 04.01.01's decision, not this feature's. | Agent | `/create-prd-architecture`'. 04.01.01:269 (D-08) answers the product half — the post is a container, the slot is the fillable unit, each slot carries a role and a count — and 04.05.01:241 (D-07) explicitly aligns to it ('Follows 04.01.01 D-08'). What is left, the submission's foreign key and its cardinality, is a data-model decision, which is exactly what the tracked target is for.

04.03.01-structured-submission.md:198 (D-08) verified verbatim: 'Type-scoped ceiling — 0 for dep-call/urgent types, 1 for session call / crew / member-wanted, 3 for brief / A&R / audition / open call, hard platform ceiling 3.' The taxonomy is closed and platform-curated (04.01.01:265 D-04) and its twelve rows at :78-89 contain no 'A&R' type. Cross-checking the list against those rows leaves function/private hire, songwriting camp invitation, support slot, open-mic/showcase slot and General call with no ceiling. The hard ceiling of 3 gives an upper bound but not a value: a presence-shaped function gig could equally take 0 like a dep call or 3 like an audition, and the rule is explicitly type-scoped rather than defaulted.

Verified: 04.03.04-blind-review-mode.md:91 (D-02) 'Blind mode is **type-scoped** | Incoherent for dep calls ...; coherent for auditions and house/orchestral work' and :55 'Poster enables blind mode on a dep call | ... **Should not be offerable for that type.** | Type-scoped availability'. The table that carries every other type-scoped property (04.01.01:76-89, columns Origin / Date semantics / Unpaid legit? / Casting class) has no blind-mode column, and only the Audition row at :81 mentions it. 04.07:43 asserts a second coherent case ('blind if enabled (04.03.04), which is coherent here') that never reaches the taxonomy. All five verified verbatim as bare markers with no owner: 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:103 and :105 (CX-03 permission intersection and state transition conflict) and :154, :155, :156 (CX-05 permission, notification fan-out and state transition, three of five synthesis slots blank). The quantity the threshold ranges over is specified. 04.03.02-evidence-backed-application.md:38 introduces the table at :40-46 as 'Evidence types, **in descending order of strength**' and enumerates five ordered tiers (verified credit with attestor / material history / prior collaboration with the poster's network / completed engagement history / self-claimed skills). An ordered five-value vocabulary is exactly what a poster-set threshold needs — the poster picks a tier — and that is what 04.03.03:111 and 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:152-153 specify ('Evidence resolved → threshold met → audition waived or reduced. Poster-set thresholds'). The absence of numeric weights is a scoring-model concern for a later layer, not a divergence at the vision layer.

Both files require both timezones rendered, and the two concrete artefacts agree on ordering. 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:87's own worked copy — 'Closes 00:00 21 Aug BST (that's 19:00 20 Aug your time)' — leads with the opportunity's zone and parenthesises the viewer's, which is precisely 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:246 (D-12, 'Dates render in the **opportunity's local timezone**, with the viewer's offset shown when they differ') and :90. Only the loose prose clause in the same row inverts the emphasis, and it still mandates both. An implementer following the example and the board rule converges.

Verified by grep: 'decide-by' occurs in 04.04.01, 04.04.03, 04.05.01 and 04.07, and **zero times** in 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md, the file that owns the post object. Dependents verified verbatim — 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:96 and :211 (every hold's resolve-by is 'bounded by the post's decide-by (04.01.01)'), :212 (D-06 derives the applicant's date from it), :158 (Dormant = '≥50% of the publish→decide-by window elapsed'), :160 (Abandoned = 'decide-by reached'), and :192 states the consequence itself ('Without a decide-by, D-05's forcing function has no bound'). 04.01.01's terms set at :270 (D-09) is closed and does not include it, and no open question anywhere asks for it — unlike the comparable gap at 04.05.03:260 (Q-07), which is tracked. The implementer must invent whether the composer collects a decide-by, whether it is mandatory, and its per-type default.

04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md:170 explicitly delegates the question — 'the *length* of that window is **04.04.04 Q-03**' — and 04.04.04-urgent-fill-first-accept-cascade.md:105 closes it: 'Resolved (DT-04, D-05): platform-set by urgency tier, ~3-min floor, poster may escalate not shorten', with D-05 at :97 stating the same. The residue is scoped and tracked with an owner and a live target ('What remains open is only the exact tier-to-minutes table | Agent | `/write-be-spec`'). D-07's 'a window they chose' (:251) and 'a shorter fuse' (:150) reconcile under that resolution: the poster chooses the urgency tier, and escalating urgency is what shortens the fuse.

Verified verbatim: 04.04.02-shortlist-multi-reviewer-scoring.md:69 'Default at Level 1: applicants are **not** auto-notified of shortlisting. The poster may optionally signal "still in consideration."' Against 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:212 (D-06) 'The applicant is told **a date, not a state** ... Never "you're a maybe" (raises hope, leaks a rank ...)' and 04.04.03:188 ('a "pending offer" hint would leak a shortlist rank'). 'Still in consideration' is a state and is exactly the maybe D-06 forbids. Its own Q-02 at :121 resolves the question as '✅ RESOLVED — no. Applicants are told a date, never a shortlist state' while quoting only the first half of the row, so the optional-signal clause survives unreconciled — and 04.05.04-applicant-pipeline-history.md:32 carries a Shortlisted pipeline state citing '04.04.02 Q-02 — unresolved' against a Q-02 that is resolved.

Verified: 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:70 and :216 (D-10) 'One candidate, one card, regardless of submission count', and :129 'One identity submits 50 times | ... Poster sees one card. Nothing indicates the 50'. The siblings require the opposite rendering for the multi-role case: 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:95 'Two candidacies, not a supersede ... Both live in the pipeline independently, each with its own disposition' and :96 for self-plus-band; 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:155 'Two submissions, two obligations, answered independently' with copy 'Won — keys. Still waiting — vocals.' 04.04.01 never scopes D-10 to same-role resubmission, so the queue that must render two independent decisions is specified to collapse them to one card.

The misstatement is real but it is not normative. 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md:208 is a Deep Think annotation (DT-04) narrating what 04.01.03 built, and its parenthetical 'versioned downward edits with reconfirm-or-auto-withdraw (D-05)' does misdescribe 04.01.03-compensation-spec-work-guardrails.md:211, which reads 'Silence keeps the applicant in the pool' and records 'Rejected auto-withdrawing on silence'. But all three decisions that own the semantics agree with each other — 04.01.03:211 (D-05), 04.01.01:270 (D-09, the file names itself 'the single authoritative terms-change rule') and 04.01.04:103 (D-06, 'never silently dropped, auto-withdrawn, or suspended-pending-reconfirm'). No implementer builds a state machine from a DT row's aside about a sibling file when three decisions state the rule identically.

Two normative statements, opposite, with no marker on either. 04.05.04-applicant-pipeline-history.md:55 'Applicant withdraws while an offer is live | **Allowed** ... **Entry moves to `withdrawn`**' and :98 (D-06) 'Applicants **can withdraw** ..., which **releases a live offer's fuse**'. Against 04.03.01-structured-submission.md:202 (D-12) '**Withdrawal is scoped to pre-offer states only** ... Once an offer is live the control hands to 04.04.03' and :100 '**Withdraw after an offer is live** | **Not a withdrawal — a decline** (D-12, DT-07)', with :155 (DT-07) recording that conflating the two verbs was the defect it fixed. The consequences diverge materially: 04.05.01:243 (D-09) excludes withdrawals 'from the denominator entirely', while a decline falls to #2 and carries a structured reason (04.04.03:194, :255).

Verified: 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:48 presents the vocabulary as 'deliberately few' and :54-62 enumerates seven values, with `expired` narrowly scoped at :61 to 'The applicant never answered an offer within its fuse'. A full-text scan of 04.05.01 for 'declin' returns only :152, an unrelated use ('the queue declines to fire'). Meanwhile 04.04.03-offer-acceptance.md makes declining first-class: the Declined state at :194 ('Falls to #2 (CX-02). Structured reason if given (D-11)') and D-11 at :255. 04.05.04:37 mirrors the hole ('Filled elsewhere / withdrawn / expired | Closed', no declined). Given #026, a decline cannot simply be filed as `withdrawn by applicant`, so no value in a closed vocabulary closes a declined candidacy.

Core verified: 04.05.03-won-opportunity-handoff.md:245 (D-16) 'Trigger fires at scheduled-end + 12h — not at 1am load-out' and :120 repeat it as the only fire-time rule, and :254 (Q-01) confirms '05 (engagements) and 07 (projects) are v1 targets and 17/18 are phase 2+'. The finding is overstated on scope: 04.01.01:78-89 classes Crew and Camp invitation as venue-local wall-clock presence types, so they do have a scheduled end — only Session call (:79) and Brief / RFP (:82) are absolute-deadline delivery types. Those two are exactly the v1-target rows (:53 → 07, :54 → 05), and for them 'scheduled-end' has no referent, leaving the domain's self-described most load-bearing mechanism (DT-07 at :198) without a fire time on the two handoffs that exist at launch. Held at warning on the corrected, narrower scope.
